applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 8 (often about ages 13-14) onto that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.text: Grade 8 Florida ELA has no foundational-reading benchmarks and no ELA.8.C.1.1. ELA.8.C.5.2 on the grade page has no terminal period. Those are Florida's grade list, not an MYP decision. Do not treat Grade 8 as a named MYP year.

official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Developing and applying these social, thinking, research, communication and self management skills helps students learn how to learn.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Middle Years Programme (MYP) language and literature courses develop skills in six areas: listening, speaking, reading, writing, viewing and presenting.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Inquiry is at the heart of MYP language learning, and aims to support students’ understanding by providing them with opportunities to independently and collaboratively investigate, take action and reflect on their learning.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: MYP language and literature courses offer a study of a wide range of literary and non-literary text types, writing styles and techniques, allowing students to comment on the significance of any possible contexts, audiences, purpose, and the use of linguistic and literary devices.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The language and literature subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Analysing; B Organizing; C Producing text; D Using language. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 8 Florida ELA in this draft asks students to analyze how character, setting, and plot interact, analyze two or more themes, analyze how authors individualize characters' perspectives, and analyze structure, sound, imagery, and figurative language in poetry; to analyze how sections convey purpose and meaning, analyze central ideas, explain purpose through rhetorical appeals and figurative language, and track an argument's reasoning and how it could be improved; to analyze figurative language and symbolism, paraphrase, compare archetypes, and explain how rhetorical devices advance an appeal. Students also write narratives with a point of view, arguments that rebut a counterclaim, and expository texts from multiple sources, follow grade-level conventions, research with multiple sources and further questions, present orally with credible evidence, and use digital tools to collaborate. MYP language and literature uses the six skill areas and four criteria above. It does not assign those Florida sentences to a grade or to an MYP year.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Analyzing the interaction of character development, setting, and plot can sit under criterion A Analysing. That interaction is a Florida demand, not an IB objective.
Analyzing how an author individualizes characters' perspectives lines up with perspective as an example key concept. MYP does not require that wording.
Explaining purpose through rhetorical appeals and figurative language can connect to criterion A Analysing. Those appeals are Florida's, not printed MYP criteria.
Tracking an argument, the types of reasoning used, and how the argument could be improved can connect to thinking skills and criterion A. Florida's sequence is the state benchmark.
Comparing archetypes across texts is a Florida benchmark. The public MYP pages retrieved do not name archetypes.
Writing a position that supports a claim and rebuts at least one counterclaim fits criterion C Producing text. The rebuttal rule, evidence rules, and organization are Florida's.
Research that draws on multiple reliable and valid sources, and that generates further questions, fits research skills. Florida's reliability rule is the state benchmark, not an IB outcome.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
